newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's parliament spurns government penal plan.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's parliament spurns government penal plan.

text.p: Portugal's minority Socialist government has suffered an embarrassing political defeat with parliament spurning its plans for penal reform.
The bill was rejected on Thursday night when all the opposition parties united to vote against the measure in the legislature where the government is four votes short of an absolute majority.
The defeat does not put at risk the future of the government, which has been in power since October 1995, but it is certain to further sour the political atmosphere.

Prime Minister Antonio Guterres recently threatened to push for early elections if the opposition, and in particular his main rivals, the conservative Social Democrats, went ahead with draft laws to boost funding for local authorities.
The row over local government funding has still not been resolved. General elections are not due in Portugal until 1999.
The government's plans to reform the penal code included wider powers for magistrates to suspend prison sentences for minor offences and the toughening of laws against sexual abuse of children.
The Social Democrats and the small right-wing Popular Party spurned the plan because they said that it was not harsh enough on criminals.
The Communists, who like the Popular Party have 15 seats in the 230-seat legislature, objected to clauses that would have made it an offence to block roads during industrial protests.
